Main_Finding: Physical inactivity, diet, and stress are significant risk factors for cardiovascular diseases (CHD). Modifiable risk factors include obesity, high blood pressure, and high serum cholesterol, while nonmodifiable factors include age, gender, and heredity. Insulin resistance, often linked to obesity and poor diet, plays a central role in metabolic syndrome, increasing the risk of hypertension and type 2 diabetes.
Practical_Application: Implement a progressive jogging program starting with 10-second jogging intervals and gradually increasing to continuous jogging. Incorporate dynamic warm-ups and cool-downs. Monitor heart rate to ensure adherence to the target heart rate (THR) zone. Encourage participation in group activities but emphasize skill matching to prevent imbalances.
Low_Resource_Applicability: Encourage walking, household chores, and community-based activities for older adults without access to specialized equipment. Suggest prenatal yoga and swimming for pregnant women. Promote school-based physical education and access to calcium-rich foods for adolescents.

Title: Perceived Exertion and Personality Traits During Different Exercise Intensities
Main_Finding: Extraversion and behavioral inhibition system (BIS) were significantly correlated with ratings of perceived exertion (RPE) during moderate-intensity exercise, while behavioral activation system (BAS) showed a negative correlation during low-intensity exercise.
Practical_Application: Coaches can consider individual differences in personality traits when communicating exercise intensity expectations and monitoring effort perception during training sessions.
Low_Resource_Applicability: Coaches can observe changes in RPE during training sessions to infer individual differences in tolerance for different exercise intensities without needing advanced monitoring tools.
Coaching_Principles: Individual differences influence perceptual responses to exercise intensity.
Constraints: Avoid applying blanket intensity prescriptions without considering individual differences in personality and perceived exertion.
Decision_Rules: IF a rider reports consistently lower RPE at higher intensities, THEN gradually increase training load while monitoring for signs of fatigue.
